Interface IuOidcActor

All Superinterfaces:
IuOidcNameClaims
public interface IuOidcActor extends IuOidcNameClaims
The act claim: who is really behind a token issued for somebody else.

Set only when a token exchange is honored, and then on both tokens. The two carry different amounts of it: an access token names the actor and when they authenticated, since a resource server needs to know an action was delegated and not who the delegate is, while an ID token adds name and email so a relying party can show its user whose session they are looking through. Every claim here is the actor's own, never the subject's — which is what RFC 8693 §4.1 means by claims within act pertaining only to the identity of the current actor.

getAuthTime() is here rather than beside the subject's own claims for that reason. An exchanged token's subject never authenticated — a caller named them, and this provider was willing to say so — so a top-level auth_time would assert something untrue about them. The actor did authenticate, and this is when.

A bean, so a token builder renders it as the nested object RFC 8693 defines rather than as a string. Optional claims are omitted from the rendering when they answer null, which is what makes one interface serve both tokens.

One interface, read and written

A provider renders an act claim from this and a relying party reads one back through it — deliberately the same type, so the two halves cannot drift apart on what an actor is. Nothing is gained by splitting a defaulted "reading" view off a required "writing" one: a claim read back arrives through a JSON proxy, which answers null for a key the object does not carry whether the accessor is default or not, so the distinction would exist only for the handful of beans a provider builds in-process.

The name claims are inherited rather than restated, so an actor is named the same way anybody else is. Only what a provider actually populates is required here; the rest answer null until one does.

See Also:

    • getAuthTime

      Long getAuthTime()
      Gets the time the actor authenticated.

      Carried on both tokens, so a relying party has an authentication age to enforce a maximum against even though the subject of an exchanged token has no authentication of their own to measure.

      Returns:
      auth_time claim, as a NumericDate — seconds since the epoch, the same as auth_time is spelled anywhere else; null when the exchanged token recorded none

    • getAcr

      String getAcr()
      Gets the authentication context class the actor's authentication satisfied.

      OpenID Connect §2 leaves acr values to agreement between the parties using them; IU's provider writes the authenticating authority's unique identifier — a federated SAML identity provider's entity ID, where a deployment authenticates that way.

      It belongs to the actor for the same reason getAuthTime() does. An exchanged token's subject never authenticated, so no authority of theirs exists to name and the token carries no top-level acr; the actor did authenticate, and this is who said so.

      Returns:
      acr claim; null when the actor's own token named no authority
      See Also:
      • OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §2
